chunks: Await the judgement of your Lord, for you are always before Our eyes, and glorify your Lord with praises when you rise,

key_terms.بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ: with the praise of your Lord

ai.seo_question: What does the command 'Sabbihi bihamdi rabbika' mean in Surah Al-Mudaththir?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Al-Mudaththir, this verse serves as a divine reassurance to the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) during the early Meccan period, affirming that his patience in delivering the message is under God's direct observation ('bi-a'yunina'). Shia scholarship often highlights the phrase 'bi-a'yunina' as indicating a special, continuous divine watchfulness over the Prophet, linking his ritual glorization (tasbih) to the broader concept of divine proximity and guidance.
